text:
A: Alright? You're the one with the dog, yeah?
B: Erm, yeah. Hiya. I'm Bethany.
A: Callum. She there now? The dog?
B: She's asleep. She's always asleep. She's called Mabel.
A: Mabel. Love that. Proper old lady name.
B: Ha. Yeah. She sort of acts like one as well.
A: Where's that to, then? Where are you?
B: Sorry? Oh, Pontefract. Yorkshire.
A: Nice. I'm Plymouth. Bit of a trek. How you finding these calls, then?
B: Erm, okay. I was dead nervous at first. It's getting a bit easier.
A: You're doing fine. I just chat rubbish, me. What do you do?
B: I was a florist. The shop shut, so... not really anything at the minute. I'm looking.
A: Ah, that's a shame. Flowers, though, that's like a proper skill, yeah? Weddings and that?
B: Yeah, weddings, funerals. I still do bits for friends. And I press flowers and frame them. Them on the shelf behind me.
A: Wait, you made them? I thought they were from a shop or something.
B: No, they're mine. Thank you.
A: Mate, you could sell them. Honestly. I flip trainers on Vinted, made forty quid on some Jordans last week. People pay stupid money for handmade stuff. Etsy, Instagram, whatever.
B: That's what the girl from Derby said, actually. Lauren. I spoke to her before.
A: Oh, Lauren! I had her first. She was a laugh. I told her to flog her windbreaker.
B: Ha, she said she weren't selling it.
A: Yeah, she weren't having it. But seriously, you should. Take a nice picture, stick it up, see what happens.
B: I don't know. It's the money side and the posting and, erm, websites. I get a bit overwhelmed. I'm not very organised, sorry.
A: Nah, you're alright. I'm not organised either, I just wing it. I've had like four extensions at uni this year.
B: Four? Do they let you?
A: If you ask nicely, yeah. I'm doing business and management, second year. Don't tell my mum about the extensions, she thinks I'm a genius.
B: Ha. I won't. Is it good, the course?
A: It's alright. Bit boring. I'm kind of not sure, to be honest. I work at a pub as well, weekends, so I'm proper knackered by Monday.
B: My husband's on nights this week. He's the same, he just sleeps all day like Mabel.
A: Ha, him and the dog. What's for your tea, then? Everyone keeps asking that on these.
B: Erm, sausage and mash. Or banana bread. I made one and it sank.
A: Banana bread for tea, that's a power move, that.
B: Ha. What about you?
A: Whatever Mum makes. If it's salad, I'm getting Greggs. Or an air fryer job, I can—
